rows.text: The categories listed in Annex I, Part A (Regulation, Article 25(2)) are the ones that always need a notified-body procedure, namely modules B, G or H or module C followed by B. Annex I, Part B categories may instead use internal production control (module A), so they are not always covered.

conformity based on full quality assurance (module H)

rows.text: For machinery in Annex I, Part A, under Article 25(2) the manufacturer must apply one of these procedures: EU type-examination (module B) followed by internal production control (module C) under option (a), full quality assurance (module H), or unit verification (module G).

value: Safety components with fully or partially self-evolving behaviour (annex I part A point 5)
rows.text: A safety component with self-evolving behaviour falls under the category of safety components with fully or partially self-evolving behaviour in Annex I, Part A, point 5.

Under Annex I, point 1.3.8.1 of the Directive and Annex III, point 1.3.8.1 of the Regulation, guards for moving transmission parts must be interlocking movable guards where frequent access is envisaged.

value: Risks related to moving parts
rows.text: Essential requirement 1.3.7 of Annex III addresses risks related to moving parts.

rows.value: The natural or legal person who carries out the substantial modification is subject to the manufacturer's obligations in Article 10 (where the impact is on the safety of only machinery or a related product forming part of an assembly of machinery).
rows.text: Under Article 18 of the Machinery Regulation, the natural or legal person carrying out a substantial modification is treated as the manufacturer and must meet the Article 10 manufacturer obligations, where the modification affects only the safety of machinery or a related product that is part of an assembly of machinery.

rows.text: Machinery placed on the market must be accompanied by the EC/EU declaration of conformity and by instructions, including the instruction manual or instructions for use in the language the Member State requires (Dir Annex I 1.7.4; Reg Art. 10(7), 10(8), 13(4), 15(2)). Where size or nature prevents this, an accompanying document is used instead (Reg Art. 10(5)).

The manufacturer must keep the technical documentation and the EU declaration of conformity for at least 10 years after the machinery or related product has been placed on the market or put into service (Art. 10(3); also Art. 12(2)).
Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 applies generally from 20 January 2027, although specified Articles apply from earlier dates.

Yes. Under point 6 of the Corrigendum, machinery placed on the market in conformity with Directive 2006/42/EC before 20 January 2027 may still be placed on the market on 16 January 2027, because the Directive is repealed only from 20 January 2027.

The DEMAG overhead travelling crane at IGEA position 8 must be verified every year (P1Y), under DLgs 81/2008 Allegato VII, riga 12, because it is a fixed crane over 200 kg used in the quarry sector and built more than 10 years ago. Assumptions of the rule: truck cranes and mobile cranes are treated as mobile, overhead and gantry cranes and hoists as fixed, and the site's sector applies to every device.

The truck-mounted hydraulic crane (device 7, capacity 790 kg, mining sector) must be verified once a year, per Annex VII row 12 of Legislative Decree 81/2008 (fact 7). Assumptions of the rule: truck cranes and mobile cranes are treated as mobile, overhead and gantry cranes and hoists as fixed, and the site's sector applies to every device.

rows.value: The ASL (Azienda Sanitaria Locale) carries out the periodic verifications after the first one.
rows.text: Under DM2011, art. 2, c. 1, the subsequent periodic verifications of the equipment listed in Allegato VII are carried out by the ASL, while the first one is carried out by INAIL.
